course_name_original: Criptografía y Codificación de la Información
prerequisites: Notions of algorithm design and analysis

learning_outcomes.text: Know the techniques of computer security that allow maintaining privacy, confidentiality and integrity in access to data and knowledge, including the basic concepts of cryptography.
Know the language and interpret concepts and parameters involved in Cryptography and Coding.
Understand the objectives of Error Correcting Codes Theory and Cryptography.
Recognize the presence and importance of error-correcting codes and encryption systems in solving real-world digital security problems.
Identify different families and classical code constructions and build error-correcting codes with specific parameters.
Manipulate encryption systems, both public and private key, and recognize situations for using some cryptosystems over others, as well as other cryptographic protocols.
Handle symbolic calculation programs for manipulating the elements involved in Code Theory and Cryptography.

syllabus_topics: Mathematical foundations of Cryptography and Coding.
Public key cryptography and digital signatures.
Introduction to error detecting and correcting codes.
Linear codes. Generator and parity-check matrix. Code parameters.
Cyclic codes: Reed-Solomon and BCH codes.
Other codes. Real applications of Code Theory.

assessment_methods.method: Attendance / Participation in Seminars and Tutoring (includes online)
Active Participation in Forums and Virtual Campus Activities

assessment_rules: The final grade (NF) in the ordinary call is calculated as: NF = 0.05 NA + 0.2 NC + 0.5 NP + 0.25 NT, where NA is the note for attendance/participation, NC for forum participation, NP for practical reports/exams, and NT for the objective theoretical-practical test. All grades are out of 10 points. The course is passed if NF >= 5. For students with officially recognized differentiated evaluation, or in extraordinary calls, the subject will be evaluated by a single final objective theoretical-practical test with a weighting of 100% (NF = NT).
